meta.note: Compiled from kalaari.com page metadata surfaced through web search plus press coverage (YourStory, Inc42, Entrackr, Forbes India, Business Standard, Tracxn/Crunchbase summaries). kalaari.com itself was not directly fetchable from the build environment, so every field carries a source list. Founder ages are 'reported' only where a dated public source states an age; otherwise they are estimated from graduation year or career length and marked as such.

firm.name: Kalaari Capital
firm.hq: Ground Floor, Unit-2, Navigator Building, ITPB, Whitefield Road, Bengaluru 560066

history.event: Founded in Bengaluru as Indo-US Venture Partners (IUVP) by Vani Kola with Vinod Dham; Fund I.
Fund II raised (~$160M, closed as $150M+ in 2012); early bets in e-commerce, edtech, SaaS, gaming.
Rebranded as Kalaari Capital; began operating Fund II in September 2012.
Fund III (~$290M) closed; Kalaari becomes one of India's largest early-stage funds.
Kstart seed fund + accelerator launched (19 companies, incl. WinZO and RED.Health).
Fund IV anchored by Reliance Industries via Jio Platforms ($100M committed, $200M total); CXXO launched for women founder-CEOs; Kalaari Fellowship follows in 2023.
'India Alpha: The Techade of Opportunity' report; portfolio tilts to vertical AI, DeepTech, SpaceTech.
Bluestone IPO (NSE/BSE, Aug), Vyome lists on Nasdaq as HIND (Aug), Jumbotail turns unicorn (Jun); 18 new investments in the year.
Continued AI-native deployment: HireBound, Articulus, FANON, NudgeBee, Mozark Series B; 20th anniversary.

thesis.oneLiner: Empower visionary entrepreneurs to build unique solutions that reshape how Indians live, work, consume and transact.
thesis.chequeRange: $500K – $5M first cheque; follow-ons in breakout companies
thesis.geography: India-first (Bengaluru HQ); global-from-India SaaS and DeepTech welcome
thesis.role: Aims to be the first institutional investor; leads or co-leads most rounds
founderFilter: Potential over pedigree: first-time founders explicitly welcome
Founder–market fit: earned insight into a deep, narrow, high-value problem
Speed to value, not just speed to launch (the 'compression effect')
Clear, compelling solution to a real-world problem

sectorFocusFundIV.why: Most recent AI bets are domain-specific: cloud ops, recruiting, hospital front desks, contracts, design.
Digantara, Chara, Peer Robotics, Articulus, Clean Electric; 'India Alpha' report names deep tech as a superpower lever.

thesis.howToPitch: Online form at kalaari.com/pitch (deck as PDF link on Drive/DocSend). Warm intros preferred, not required. Expect a reply within a few weeks. Deck should cover business model, market, financials and team.

reports.title: India Alpha: The Techade of Opportunity
reports.takeaway: India as a $30T economy by 2047; healthcare to $401B by 2030; factories lose $50B/yr to downtime that AI-native tools can recover.

reports.title: Wired for Impact: Women in (Ind)AI
reports.takeaway: AI/ML is the top career track for women in tech (41% vs 37% for men); women are 1 in 5 of India's tech workforce; 3.3 lakh women expected in AI roles by 2027.

reports.title: Gameconomy '23
reports.takeaway: Primer on India's gaming opportunity (Harshit Kumar).

programs.name: CXXO
programs.what: Capital, community and coaching for women founder-CEOs. $10M per year for 8–10 companies, each matched with a champion advisor. Build-It launchpad with Harappa.

programs.name: Kstart
programs.what: Seed fund + accelerator; invested via convertible instruments, ~$500K per company, quarterly batches. 19 companies, 5 acquisitions (Perpule → Amazon, Square Off → Miko, Parablu, Active.ai → Gupshup).

programs.name: Kalaari Fellowship
programs.what: Two-year, full-time apprenticeship into venture. Year 1: analytical rigour (₹1 lakh/month stipend); Year 2: closer to deal-making. For professionals with 1–6 years' experience. 2026 applications open.

programs.name: Alpha Archives
programs.what: Insights hub: The Kalaari Podcast, The Hindsight (Vani Kola with founders), Changemakers (20-year series), SaaS from Scratch, Web3 Talks, Hindustan Hamara, Why-We-Invested notes.
